macOS · USB HCI · SwiftUI

Raw Bluetooth

An experimental userspace driver that uses an external USB Bluetooth adapter and Google Bumble to connect keyboards and mice to macOS. A SwiftUI app handles scanning, pairing, and saved devices.

Why I built it

I wanted to use Bluetooth keyboards and mice with an external USB adapter through a dedicated macOS app.

How input reaches macOS

  1. The app talks to the external adapter over USB HCI.
  2. Google Bumble discovers and pairs Bluetooth Low Energy devices.
  3. The driver decodes HID reports and forwards keyboard and mouse events to macOS.

Test setup

I tested a CSR USB adapter (0a12:0001), a Logitech M196 mouse, and a Logitech K250 keyboard on Intel macOS. Audio remains experimental.
